principles.statement: Start meaningful speaking near A0 with short bounded production; do not make open conversation the gate to having a speaking curriculum.
Progress speaking demand from rehearsal to independent retrieval, controlled recombination, guided interaction and only later sampled open interaction.
Store listen-and-repeat, shadowing and read-aloud as rehearsal evidence; never silently promote model-visible performance to independent speaking evidence.
Allow planning and lexical/chunk support to reduce beginner speaking load, but hide answer-bearing language before an independent attempt and record planning/support provenance.
Match each speaking claim to its response demand: a productive claim requires oral retrieval and an interaction claim requires a contingent response to another turn.
Use standardized guided Q&A, information-gap or role-play tasks to introduce interaction before relying on unrestricted AI conversation as the primary beginner measure.
Use oral task repetition to rehearse and proceduralize performance, but require a changed or unseen task for fresh speaking-transfer evidence.
Increase speaking difficulty progressively and avoid stacking new content, new language, new interlocutor demands and open response freedom at the same time for near-A0 learners.
After an independent speaking error, prefer a short opportunity for self-repair when plausible; if repair fails, reveal/correct and treat the following repetition as supported relearning.
Do not equate faster or longer speech with global speaking mastery; fluency measures are task-conditioned evidence alongside task success, language form and interaction evidence.
Do not use opaque ASR or pronunciation scores as speaking mastery gates before RQ-007/RQ-008 establish target validity and scoring reliability for the intended population.
Calibrate speaking progression against delayed success on first-seen parallel production tasks per learner minute and burden, not immediate rehearsal smoothness alone.
